artifacts.summary: Confirms the three-group coverage gap; rules out both suggested extension points for NomicLanguage on structural grounds; specifies and compile-verifies four artifacts (new NomicLanguageTest + ForMathlib SmokeTest modules, two Automation folds); records the C6/C16/C28 gate obligations; and reports a measured live bug in FormalSystem/Tactic/Meta.lean's buildContextExpr.

user_decision.question: FormalSystem/Tactic/Meta.lean's buildContextExpr is broken and throws on every call (measured): its first line is `mkAppM ``List.nil #[formulaType]`, but List.nil's type argument is implicit, so mkAppM raises 'too many explicit arguments provided to @List.nil'. Its two consumers (Search.lean:475 tryModalK, Search.lean:527 tryTemporalK) call it outside their `observing?` block, so `example : |-[FrameClass.Base] box (p imp p) := by modal_search` hard-fails with that error. Repairing it requires editing a FormalSystem declaration, which this task's description places explicitly out of scope. Which do you want? (a) widen this task's scope by one objective to apply the one-line repair (two candidate repairs were compiled and both work: `mkAppOptM ``List.nil #[some formulaType]`, or `Lean.mkApp (Lean.mkConst ``List.nil [Level.zero]) formulaType`); (b) keep this task's scope as written -- the item (C) probe then #checks buildContextExpr without invoking it -- and spawn a separate task for the repair; or (c) keep scope and leave the repair unfiled.
options: (a) widen scope by one objective and apply the pre-validated one-line repair here
(b) keep scope; spawn a separate task for the repair (research's default recommendation)
(c) keep scope; leave the repair unfiled
user_decision.recommendation: (b) -- the repair is a genuine FormalSystem bug fix, not a testability change, so it deserves its own task record rather than being folded into a test-coverage task; the pre-validated fix makes that follow-up cheap.
